title: Short Stuff: Marianne Bachmeier: Vigilante Mother
summary: Short Stuff installment on Marianne Bachmeier, the German mother who shot and killed Klaus Grabowski in open court in Lübeck (West Germany) in 1981, during his trial for the sexual assault and murder of her seven-year-old daughter Anna. The hosts cover the crime, the courtroom shooting, public reaction and a 1983 Allensbach Institute survey on the sentence, her manslaughter conviction and three-year sentence, her later life in Nigeria and Sicily, her 1995 admission that the killing was premeditated, her death from pancreatic cancer in 1996, and her burial beside her daughter.

segments.title: Opening and introduction
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Short Stuff episode on vigilante justice, sitting in for Dave with Chuck, and names the sources used.

segments.title: Anna's abduction and murder
segments.summary: Hosts describe the case: seven-year-old Anna Bachmeier was abducted in May 1980 by Klaus Grabowski, a 35-year-old butcher on probation with a history of crimes against children, and was sexually assaulted and strangled, her body discarded in a canal.

segments.title: Grabowski trial and courtroom shooting
segments.summary: Grabowski was turned in by his fiancée and put on trial. His defense claimed Anna threatened to accuse him unless he paid her, and Marianne Bachmeier then shot him in court on day three with a smuggled .22 Beretta, hitting him six times and killing him.

segments.title: Public reaction and criticism of her character
segments.summary: Many people supported the killing, and about 100,000 Deutsche Marks were raised for her defense. Some criticized her past, including having two children out of wedlock that she adopted out, and her later marriage and job in a pub.

segments.title: Conviction, sentence and debate over leniency
segments.summary: Bachmeier was convicted of manslaughter and unlawful possession of a firearm and served three years of a six-year sentence. A 1983 Allensbach Institute survey found views split on the sentence. The case sparked debate about repeat offenders and whether a parent may kill to avenge a child.

segments.title: Later life, admission and death
segments.summary: Bachmeier was released in June 1985 and moved to Nigeria, where she married and later divorced. She later developed pancreatic cancer in Sicily, returned to Germany, and in a mid-1990s TV interview admitted the killing was premeditated. She died in 1996 at 46, and the hosts note she had reportedly been sexually abused as a child.

segments.title: Burial and closing thoughts
segments.summary: Bachmeier was buried beside her daughter at Burgtor Cemetery in Lübeck, and the hosts reflect on the case and the moral debate.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the Short Stuff episode and the show's production credit is read.
